clue.text: Convertible frequently involved in finish

indicators.note: one word is wrapped up inside another, so frequently sits within finish

parts.note: to finish is to stop
oft is the poetic word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A car with a folding roof keeps cropping up at the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with a soft folding roof is called a convertible, the roof being collapsible fabric.

clue.text: Gateway set in small farm building is very stiff

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another, so the gateway sits within the farm building

parts.note: a sty is a small building for pigs
an arch can form a gateway

explanation.surface: An entrance placed in a pigsty is extremely rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy means stiff and formal, like a collar stiffened with starch.

clue.text: Woman ensnaring endless chaps with lots of dough

definitions.text: Woman ensnaring endless chaps with lots of dough

indicators.note: one piece traps another inside it, so the woman word goes round the rest

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for chaps goes

parts.note: chaps are men
dough is money, and a fat sum is a lot of it

explanation.surface: A seductress catches men by the dozen, and plenty of their money too.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a gold-digger: the seductress only snares the men who are rich, so the whole clue also defines her, an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A femme fatale is a seductive woman who lures men to their ruin.

clue.text: Advice to English: go quietly

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A suggestion to the English to leave without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the tips of one's toes is to move silently, so it means go quietly.

clue.text: Tendency to ask questions about blatant lie

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, so the questioning word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to pry is to ask nosy questions
open can mean blatant, done without concealment
to lie somewhere is to sit there, as a town lies or sits on a river

explanation.surface: An inclination to question an obvious falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like a falsehood, but it is the verb, to rest or sit. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A propensity is a natural inclination or tendency to behave in a certain way.

clue.text: Composer is hardly in debt to the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the spoken sound, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: someone hardly in debt barely owes anything

explanation.surface: A musician who has scarcely any debts, as listeners are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'barely owes' sounds like the name of the French Romantic composer Hector Berlioz.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a nineteenth-century French composer of the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Vessel with second-class set of sails

parts.note: B grade is second class, after A
a ship's rig is its arrangement of masts and sails

explanation.surface: A ship has a second-rate suit of sails.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Cashed in first of bonds not needed in desirable conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
something is not needed inside a word, so a letter is removed
only the opening letter of the word bonds is taken

explanation.surface: Someone has cashed in their bonds in an attractive conversion deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not needed in' removes B (first of bonds) from DESIRABLE, leaving DESIRALE; 'conversion' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to sell it for cash, so realised means cashed in.

clue.text: Ruling party starts to introduce National Service

indicators.note: the starts, or first letters, of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: The governing party starts to bring in National Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins is an idiom for those in office, the party in power, as opposed to the outs.

clue.text: Yellow mineral Zambia initially needs to promote

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the word Zambia is taken

parts.note: to incite is to stir up or promote

explanation.surface: An African country first needs to push its mineral exports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Zincite is a zinc oxide mineral, typically orange-red to yellow in colour.

clue.text: A jolly weapon?

parts.note: a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Is a cheerful thing a weapon, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, but in crosswords it is a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM. The question mark flags that an arm as weapon is a slightly stretched sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a single firearm can be called an arm.

clue.text: Wanderer returning for excavation further north

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a dig is an archaeological excavation
further, as in moreover, means also

explanation.surface: Someone coming back from a dig in the northern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the parable in Luke's gospel of the son who wanders off, squanders his inheritance and comes home.
explanation.definitionFit: The prodigal son of the Bible parable leaves home, wastes everything and comes back forgiven.

clue.text: Indian woman's agreement to be seen in church, up to a point

indicators.note: one part appears inside another, so the words sit within church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
her is the possessive for a woman
OK expresses agreement
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A Native American woman nods yes in church, to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to' simply joins the point onto the end. 'Indian' here means a Native American, not someone from India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people, once commonly called American Indians.

clue.text: Left one holding pine tree

parts.note: to pine for something is to long or itch for it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remaining specimen grows a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning to long for. The clue reads L, I, then holding a piece; the letters actually run L, ITCH, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, or lychee, is an Asian fruit tree grown for its sweet fruit.

clue.text: Herb's touring French city to find composer

indicators.note: one piece goes round, touring, another, so the herb surrounds the city

parts.note: chives are a herb
Arles is a city in Provence, southern France

explanation.surface: Herb takes a trip round a French city to track down a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Herb's is a link (Herb has to find); the herb word surrounds the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer, known for The Unanswered Question.

clue.text: In which one is apart, sadly

definitions.text: In which one is apart, sadly

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A state where a person is alone and unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ONE IS APART rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Separation is a state of being apart, often sadly, as a couple living apart.

clue.text: Surely energy's needed in revolutionary dance

indicators.note: one piece is needed inside another, so energy goes within the dance word
something revolutionary turns round, so the dance word is read backwards

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rebellious dance certainly calls for plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns HAY round to YAH; E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal yes of agreement, as in 'yes, certainly', which is close to saying surely.

clue.text: Declare, since quite a few short of length trap everyone in front

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

indicators.note: missing something, so a letter for length is dropped

parts.note: several means quite a few

indicators.note: the fronts of the words trap and everyone are taken, their first letters

explanation.surface: Someone states that, lacking a long few, the trap catches everyone ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of length' and 'in front' are the two signals; the comma after Declare marks off the definition, and 'trap' and 'everyone' give letters only, not meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is a formal word meaning to declare or assert solemnly.

clue.text: She's found quickly in alphabetical list of stars

definitions.note: she is, with the 's a link: the nymph of Greek myth set among the stars as the Great Bear

indicators.note: the answer can be found, quickly or not, inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A celebrity is easy to look up in an A-to-Z directory of famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across alphabetiCAL LIST Of. 'stars' completes the picture: in myth the nymph was set in the sky as Ursa Major, though the name is better known now for a moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this nymph, loved by Zeus, was turned into a bear and placed in the sky.

clue.text: Pervert taking heroin out of metal butt-holder

parts.note: lead is a metal

indicators.note: something taken out of another word, so the heroin letter goes

parts.note: an ashtray holds cigarette butts
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A deviant takes drugs from a metal ashtray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' is the verb, to corrupt, not the noun. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert someone is to corrupt them, to lead them astray from the right path.

clue.text: Very different flights will end in this

definitions.text: Very different flights will end in this

parts.words: Very different flights will end in this
parts.note: flights of stairs end on a level floor, and aeroplane flights end on touching down: two very different kinds

explanation.surface: Two quite different kinds of flight finish in the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flights' means both a flight of stairs and a journey by air; both end in the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase leads to a level floor of that name, and an aircraft's flight ends by coming down.

clue.text: Black rim often seen on radar screen

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: A dark edge is a common sight on a radar display.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is the small spot of light marking a detected object on a radar display.

clue.text: Usual small part revised by playwright

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PT is a short form of part

explanation.surface: A dramatist reworks his usual minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges USUAL with PT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plautus was a Roman comic playwright whose plays inspired later farce.

clue.text: Showman bringing pitmen to pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers, the pitmen's union

explanation.surface: An entertainer takes the coal miners down to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' sets the miners after the pub. NUM is the British miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: P.T. Barnum was the American showman behind Barnum's American Museum and circus.

clue.text: Syringe found in sledge?

definitions.meaning: a hypodermic syringe is fitted with a fine hollow point for injecting
in cricket, to sledge is to taunt a batsman verbally, to goad or provoke them

explanation.walkthrough: 'sledge' looks like the snow vehicle; in cricket slang it means to taunt a batsman, as needle does. 'found in' is a link, and the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the sharp point on a syringe, and the verb meaning to goad someone.

clue.text: Issue of Atlas covering situations in Eastern state

indicators.note: one piece covers another, so the situations word sits within

parts.note: Maia was one of the Pleiades, daughters of the Titan Atlas in Greek myth
the lay of the land is its situation, so lays are situations

explanation.surface: A new edition of a map book includes various places in an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like an edition of an atlas, but it means offspring: Maia, a daughter of the Titan Atlas. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia is a federation in South-East Asia, so it is a state in the East.

clue.text: One wearing blue is climbing platform

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads upwards, so the letters go backwards
the one is wearing the blue, so the letters sit together with one inside

parts.note: blue means sad, depressed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single gloomy person is going up onto a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside SAD to make SIAD; 'climbing' turns it round. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform at one end of a hall, for speakers or guests.

clue.text: A nit is often the product of this

definitions.text: A nit is often the product of this

indicators.note: the letters produce something new when rearranged, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A louse egg usually comes from a plague of lice.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A NIT IS OFTEN rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: a nit comes from a plague of lice.
explanation.definitionFit: An infestation of lice in the hair is what leaves nits, the eggs, behind.

clue.text: Flower's to die, but not completely

definitions.note: flower is, with the 's a link: a flower is a river, a thing that flows

indicators.note: not complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to fall in battle is to die

explanation.surface: A bloom is going to wilt, but not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crosswordese for a river, something that flows; the Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, and a river is a flower in the sense of one that flows.

clue.text: Scrutinise old soldier

definitions.meaning: to scrutinise something is to examine or check it carefully
US short form of veteran, a former member of the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to check something carefully, and short for a veteran of the forces.

clue.text: Type of humour gravity at first permits

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word gravity is taken

parts.note: permits means allows

explanation.surface: Some kind of comedy is first allowed by seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a modifier: the answer is the word before 'humour' in the grim kind of joking about death.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallows humour is grim joking about death and disaster, named after the hangman's scaffold.

clue.text: Goddess seems in trouble

indicators.note: letters put in trouble are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deity appears to be having difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in trouble' but is fodder: SEEMS IN is the anagram, 'trouble' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, punishing hubris.
